_comment: Starter config. Edit and save; padctl reloads live, no restart. A typo keeps the last good config instead of crashing. Everything here is herdr-free, so it works on a plain Mac. If you use herdr, see the `keys`/`text`/`workspace` actions, which target a herdr pane.

_actions.keys: { type: keys, keys: [enter, ctrl+u, shift+tab, esc, up, ...] } -> focused herdr pane, NOT system-wide
_actions.text: { type: text, text: <string>, submit: true|false } -> focused herdr pane
_actions.workspace: { type: workspace, dir: next|prev } -> herdr workspaces
_actions.hotkey: { type: hotkey, key: enter|escape|a-z|0-9|<code>, modifiers: [command,shift,option,control] } -> SYSTEM-WIDE, works in any app
_actions.click: { type: click, button: left|right } -> SYSTEM-WIDE click
_actions.hold: { type: hold, button: left|right } -> SYSTEM-WIDE. Down on press, up on release: tap = click, keep held = drag.

_controls: south east west north dpad_up dpad_down dpad_left dpad_right l1 r1 l2 r2 l3 r3 menu view touchpad lstick_up lstick_down lstick_left lstick_right rstick_up rstick_down rstick_left rstick_right  (l1 is the layer modifier, never bindable)  |  touchpad swipes: swipe_left swipe_right swipe_up swipe_down
_l1: Hold L1 and press something. This layer wins everywhere, in any app.
_desktop: desktop_bindings override `bindings` whenever the frontmost app is NOT terminal_bundle. L1 always wins. Anything not listed falls back to `bindings`. Only useful once you have herdr-targeted `keys`/`text` bindings that need a system-wide counterpart.
_chords: Optional. e.g. {"l2+r2": {...}}. Both presses must land within 140ms of each other AND stay held 250ms. Any button named in a chord pays a 140ms delay on its solo action, so only chord buttons that can afford to be slow, and never put a destructive action here.

l2+r2._note: Screenshot to clipboard. Safe to chord: a stray one costs nothing.
